inspection_summary: Inspected all 381 normalized lines. The paper defines the de Bruijn-Newman threshold in terms of real versus non-real zeros, uses non-real zeros of associated Jensen polynomials as a lower-bound obstruction, replaces exhaustive root finding with Sturm real-root counts, and records the truncation, quadrature, precision, interval, and Newton-check mechanisms used to support the reported bound. Formula extraction is degraded in several displayed equations, but the selected mechanisms remain recoverable from adjacent prose; exact formula reuse requires the retained scan.

sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Front matter plus a prose summary of the lower-bound certificate, polynomial degree, high precision, Sturm sequence, and complex-zero result.

sections_inspected.label: Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines the threshold phenomenon, connects it to the Riemann hypothesis, states the prior and new lower bounds, and frames the computational difficulty.

sections_inspected.label: Algorithm and results
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Introduces moments and Jensen polynomials, states the non-real-zero obstruction, compares root-finding and Sturm approaches, gives the continuation algorithm, and reports qualitative behavior and a precision diagnostic.

accepted_units.title: The de Bruijn-Newman real-zero threshold
accepted_units.why_material: The passage organizes the problem around a parameter threshold: above it the entire functions have only real zeros, below it some zeros are non-real; it states the implications and conjectural relation to the Riemann hypothesis and frames improvement of a lower bound as the goal.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the local properties of the kernel and the threshold statements needed to interpret the lower-bound task. Equation (1), which defines the transform, is absent from the extracted text, so the unit supports the threshold logic but not exact reconstruction of the transform.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the lambda-parameterized entire-function and zero-location representation; precise notation and equation (1) require scan verification because of extraction loss.

accepted_units.title: Jensen-polynomial witness for a lower bound
accepted_units.why_material: The Taylor expansion supplies moments and associated finite-degree Jensen polynomials, and the cited criterion says that a non-real zero of one such polynomial at a chosen parameter witnesses that the parameter lies below the de Bruijn-Newman constant.
accepted_units.context_note: The prose at lines 125-136 preserves the construction's role and the obstruction criterion even though displayed equations (3) and (4) are degraded.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Uses a finite polynomial representation derived from transform moments; exact coefficient normalization is formula-sensitive and must be checked against the scan.

accepted_units.title: Earlier coefficient-error certification by full root computation
accepted_units.why_material: This passage records the prior constructive certificate: compute moments with known precision, find every polynomial zero, and use an Ostrowski error bound to transfer a numerically observed complex zero from approximate to exact coefficients. It also identifies coefficient sensitivity as the driver of very high precision.
accepted_units.context_note: Kept separately because it is the baseline method against which the paper's Sturm strategy is motivated.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on approximate polynomial coefficients, numerical root locations, and an external coefficient-perturbation theorem cited rather than reproduced here.

accepted_units.title: Count real roots instead of finding all roots
accepted_units.why_material: Anticipated growth in the first complex-root degree makes repeated computation of all zeros expensive; the paper reframes the needed decision as detecting whether any zeros are non-real and selects Sturm sequences as a cheaper route.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the central algorithmic change and its explicit cost motivation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Relies on the fact that a degree-m real polynomial has a non-real zero when a certified real-root count is smaller than m, with multiplicity conditions handled in the following setup.

accepted_units.title: Sturm sequence and sign-variation root count
accepted_units.why_material: The passage constructs a decreasing-degree polynomial sequence by Euclidean division and states that the difference of endpoint sign-variation counts equals the number of real zeros on an interval.
accepted_units.context_note: Lines 161-162 are retained because the definition begins before the page break; the simple-zero case is stated explicitly.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on polynomial remainder sequences and endpoint sign representations; several primes and subscripts are OCR-sensitive but the prose statement is recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Continuation search from a known complex zero
accepted_units.why_material: Starting from a known parameter and minimal degree, the algorithm moves to larger parameters, computes successive Jensen polynomials, counts their real zeros on a chosen interval, and then uses a tracked local extremum and the previous imaginary part to initialize Newton's method as a check. It reports minimal degrees with two missing real roots and increasingly small imaginary parts.
accepted_units.context_note: Combines the end-to-end search logic with the qualitative result pattern because the latter interprets what the procedure returns.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on parameter continuation, real-root counts over a sufficiently wide negative interval, and numerical complex-root coordinates; exact symbols are partially degraded but the procedural prose is intact.

accepted_units.title: Chaotic sign patterns diagnose insufficient precision
accepted_units.why_material: A sudden chaotic departure of the Sturm endpoint-sign sequence from the preceding degree's pattern is used as an operational warning that working precision is inadequate.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a diagnostic heuristic, not by itself a proof that the restored calculation is correct.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on comparing ordered sign sequences from consecutive Jensen-polynomial degrees at the same endpoint.

accepted_units.title: Minimal degree and precision grow sharply toward minus five
accepted_units.why_material: The table reports minimal degrees rising from 16 at parameter -50 to 406 at -5, together with complex-zero approximations and working precision, concretely supporting the paper's claim that improvement becomes much more expensive.
accepted_units.context_note: Table headings and all rows are retained so the trend is not inferred from isolated values; some spacing and decimal typography are extraction-degraded.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly table- and numeral-dependent; verify exact complex-zero digits and precision labels against the scan before quantitative reuse.

accepted_units.title: Tail-bound selection for moment integration
accepted_units.why_material: The moment integral is split at a cutoff, an analytic upper bound controls the omitted tail, and the cutoff is chosen so that this contribution is negligible relative to both the moments and the working precision; the parameter -5 computation is used as the concrete check.
accepted_units.context_note: Lines 263-272 cross a page break and jointly complete the comparison between the tail bound, the smallest reported moment, and 250-digit arithmetic.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on formula (5), an exponential tail inequality, and numerical magnitude comparisons; OCR damage to exponents requires scan verification for exact constants.

accepted_units.title: Precision-aware truncation of the kernel series
accepted_units.why_material: A remainder inequality for truncating the kernel series is used to choose the number of terms as a function of the evaluation point, requested decimal precision, and the scale of the leading term.
accepted_units.context_note: The prose preserves the adaptive selection principle and dominance argument.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The exact remainder and closed-form choice of N are formula-sensitive; radicals, exponents, and symbols in lines 276-283 need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Evenness makes trapezoidal refinement preferable to Romberg extrapolation
accepted_units.why_material: Inspection of the Romberg table showed extrapolation reducing rather than increasing accuracy, while the first-column trapezoidal estimates converged rapidly. The paper connects this to exponential convergence for an even integrand and therefore uses repeated composite-trapezoid halving with reusable precomputed values.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the empirical anomaly, the structural explanation, the resulting method choice, and the observed digit-doubling behavior.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the even-integrand representation and a cited convergence theorem whose conditions are asserted here but not reproduced.

accepted_units.title: Direct recurrence for the Sturm polynomial coefficients
accepted_units.why_material: The passage turns the abstract Sturm definition into a coefficient computation: initialize with the Jensen polynomial and its derivative, obtain initial coefficients from the moments, and apply linear-quotient remainder relations through the decreasing-degree sequence.
accepted_units.context_note: The qualitative construction is recoverable, but the displayed coefficient indices and recurrence typography are not safe enough for literal implementation from this extraction alone.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Highly formula- and subscript-dependent; exact recurrence use requires verification from the page image.

accepted_units.title: Adaptive root interval, precision escalation, and explicit-zero cross-check
accepted_units.why_material: The real-root count is performed on an interval enlarged when necessary; abrupt implausible count drops are attributed to insufficient precision and resolved by increasing accuracy. A separately computed complex zero, located through a local extremum, is retained as an extra check.
accepted_units.context_note: The paper reports this as its practical strategy; precision restoration and the explicit zero are supporting checks rather than substitutes for the Sturm count.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on negativity of the real zeros as stated here, a sufficiently wide interval, stable endpoint sign counts, and high-precision numerical evaluation.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Finite-dimensional obstruction certificate for a de Bruijn-Newman lower bound
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: At a fixed parameter, moment-derived Jensen polynomials convert the lower-bound question into finding a non-real zero; Sturm counts reduce that decision to certified real-root counting, while truncation, quadrature, interval, and precision controls support the numerical inputs and Newton supplies an extra check.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source relies on cited results for the Jensen implication and trapezoidal convergence, and several displayed formulas are extraction-degraded, so the scan and cited assumptions are required before reproducing the certificate.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Observed degree growth as the practical obstruction to stronger bounds
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Across the reported parameters, the first Jensen-polynomial degree with complex roots grows sharply as the parameter increases toward -5, with the -5 case reaching degree 406 and requiring much higher precision, matching the stated warning that further improvement by this algorithm is formidable.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is a finite computational trend and an authorial assessment, not a theorem giving asymptotic degree or complexity growth.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Layered numerical checks around the Sturm decision
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The paper moves away from full-root computation plus a coefficient-error theorem, monitors unstable Sturm sign patterns as a precision warning, restores expected counts by raising precision, and computes an explicit complex zero as an additional check.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Pattern stability and Newton convergence are diagnostic corroboration; the source does not present them as standalone substitutes for all exact error analysis.
